title: Anant Nag to Receive Dadasaheb Phalke Award; Modi Hails 'Remarkable Versatility'
excerpt: The Kannada cinema veteran, whose career spans five decades and more than 300 films, will receive Indian cinema's highest honour at the 72nd National Film Awards in Kevadia on September 22.
body:
• Veteran actor Anant Nag will receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, Indian cinema's highest honour, at the 72nd National Film Awards in Kevadia, Gujarat, on September 22.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the 78-year-old on X, calling the award a "richly deserved honour" for an artist whose "effortless performances, remarkable versatility and brilliance" left a strong mark on Indian cinema, particularly Kannada cinema.
  • Nag becomes only the second Kannada icon after Dr. Rajkumar to receive the award, and the honour follows his Padma Bhushan in 2025 — his second major national recognition in two years.

Veteran actor Anant Nag will be conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting announced on Wednesday, placing the Kannada cinema doyen alongside the immortals of Indian film.

The decision, taken on the recommendation of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award Selection Committee, recognizes Nag's illustrious cinematic journey spanning more than five decades, which the ministry said has inspired generations of artists and enriched the nation's cultural landscape. He will receive the honour from President Droupadi Murmu at the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony in Kevadia, Gujarat, on September 22.

Modi: "richly deserved honour"

Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the congratulations, posting on X: "Congratulations to the legendary Anant Nag Ji on being conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. For several decades, his effortless performances, remarkable versatility and brilliance have left a very strong mark on Indian cinema, particularly Kannada cinema. In whichever role he has played, he brought rare depth and authenticity. This is indeed a richly deserved honour for a truly distinguished artist."

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2100196542464598295

The announcement makes Nag only the second Kannada icon after Dr. Rajkumar to receive the nation's highest film prize, underscoring his status as one of the most versatile performers Indian cinema has produced.

Five decades, 300 films, parallel and mainstream

Born on September 4, 1948, Nag made his acting debut in the Kannada feature Sankalp and his Hindi debut in Shyam Benegal's Ankur, going on to portray diverse characters in more than 300 films across Kannada, Hindi, Telugu, Malayalam, Tamil and Marathi cinema. His landmark works include Minchina Ota, Hamsageethe, Ankur and Manthan, as well as the beloved television series Malgudi Days, where he played Swami's father.

Nag's career is notable for its seamless movement between parallel and mainstream cinema, and for a long association with theatre. His honours include five Filmfare Awards, five Karnataka State Best Actor Awards, the Karnataka Rajyotsava Award and an honorary doctorate from Bangalore University. In 2023 he celebrated the golden jubilee of his 50-year career in cinema.

A second national honour in two years

The Phalke Award follows the Padma Bhushan conferred on him by President Murmu in 2025, making it his second major national recognition in as many years. Responding to the announcement, Nag said: "Well, just last year I was a happy recipient of Padma Bhushan from the hands of the President... and now this has come, and the Prime Minister has tweeted. I was very happy because of that. I'm very grateful and thankful to him."

For several decades, his effortless performances, remarkable versatility and brilliance have left a very strong mark on Indian cinema, particularly Kannada cinema. — Prime Minister Narendra Modi

Dedicated to the people of Karnataka

Nag said he dedicates the honour to the people of Karnataka, just as he dedicated last year's Padma Bhushan. "The people of Karnataka have blessed me, blessed my films, supported me for the last fifty years," he told IANS. "This year I have got another opportunity to again dedicate it to the people of Karnataka — and now India — because this is for the acting award."

What's next

The formal conferral at the National Film Awards ceremony on September 22 will be a homecoming for the Kannada film industry, which has long championed Nag's case for the honour. For Kannada cinema, long seen as overshadowed nationally by Hindi and Tamil industries, the award is a moment of overdue recognition — and a reminder of how much of Indian cinema's finest acting has come from its smaller industries.
